prompts.sky: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one polished landscape 16:9 gameplay screen mockup for EPOCA, a high-quality pixel-art fantasy idle hunting RPG. Read this as a fresh game brief, unrelated to earlier sprite experiments. Premium hand-crafted pixel art with crisp deliberate pixel clusters, rich restrained colors, textured tiles, beautiful layered environments and legible small animated-looking sprites; no painting, no blurry pseudo-pixels, no 3D. Main gameplay scene occupies about 80% of screen, simple elegant dark compact pixel UI, no dashboard/card grid, no dense text panels or explanatory annotations. Show automatic hunting: a single equipment-defined adventurer fighting a small group of local creatures, a few subtle damage numbers, readable attack and hit effects, material pickup. No fixed class labels. Compact top bar with EPOCA, realm label, health and coin icons. Bottom compact equipment/skill slots and Korean navigation labels exactly "사냥터", "장비", "스킬", "도감", "거래소". Small unobtrusive "자동 사냥" status and "조사 기록" button. Adaptation should be hinted through creature appearance and combat reaction, never numerical adaptation gauges, countdowns, stage numbers, or a giant adaptation panel. No wolf, no snowfield. This is a concept proposal, not a screenshot of an implemented game. Consistent UI placement and rendering language across the realm series. Realm label exactly "하늘". An airy floating-island hunting ground above a vast sea of clouds. Broken pale stone bridges, wind-carved grass islands, hanging roots, distant floating ruins, luminous gold morning light and blue-violet shadows. Adventurer wearing a short travel cloak with a bow stands on solid island ground shooting a small winged local creature; two other birdlike creatures with layered wind-resistant feather silhouettes at different depths. Ground and flight silhouettes readable. Vertical depth and space, restrained feather-and-air impact effects. Original fantasy ecology, coherent pixel scale. No need to explain the adaptation in text.
